records.source: לֹ֥א תִשָּׂ֖א שֵׁ֣מַע שָׁ֑וְא אַל־תָּ֤שֶׁת יָֽדְךָ֙ עִם־רָשָׁ֔ע לִהְיֹ֖ת עֵ֥ד חָמָֽס׃ס
records.gloss: Not you must lift up a report of falsehood. Do not put your hand with a wicked [one] to be a witness of violence.
pieces: Do not pass along a false report. Do not join forces with a wicked person by serving as a witness whose words do violence.

L.1: You shall not take up a false report. Do not put your hand with a wicked [one] to be a witness of violence.

R.1: Do not spread untrue stories about others. Do not help a guilty person by telling lies in court that will hurt someone.

decisions.choice: take up a false report: start or spread a groundless rumor
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or carry. A false report may be lifted up by being started or carried on by being repeated, and both are forbidden. It is the same word for "false" as in the commandment about the name (20:7).

decisions.choice: put your hand with ... a witness of violence: side with the guilty by testimony that does harm
decisions.reason: To put one's hand with someone is to join him in a cause. A "witness of violence" is one whose testimony is meant to wrong another, even to take a life (Deuteronomy 19:16-19; Psalm 35:11). The ninth commandment is applied to the court (20:16).

decisions.choice: telling lies in court
decisions.reason: Readable spells out that the witness gives false testimony in a court case, as the context of verses 1-3 and 6-8 shows.

records.heading: Honest witness and fair justice

records.source: לֹֽא־תִהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרֵֽי־רַבִּ֖ים לְרָעֹ֑ת וְלֹא־תַעֲנֶ֣ה עַל־רִ֗ב לִנְטֹ֛ת אַחֲרֵ֥י רַבִּ֖ים לְהַטֹּֽת׃
records.gloss: Not you must be after many [people] to evil deeds, and not you must answer on a case at law to turn aside after many [people] to thrust aside.
pieces: Do not follow a crowd to do evil. And when you speak in a lawsuit, do not lean toward the many so as to bend justice.

L.2: You shall not be after many to do evil; and you shall not answer in a lawsuit, turning aside after many, to pervert [justice].

R.2: Do not do wrong just because many others are doing it. When you speak as a witness in court, do not go along with the crowd and make the outcome unfair.

decisions.choice: many: the majority, the crowd
decisions.reason: The word means "many". It may also mean "great ones", the powerful (Job 32:9), but the contrast with the poor in verse 3 suggests a crowd or majority, whose weight can push a witness or a judge.

decisions.choice: answer in a lawsuit ... to pervert: give testimony that bends the verdict
decisions.reason: To "answer" in a case is to testify (20:16). The last verb, to thrust aside, has no object; the sense is to turn justice away from what is right, as in verse 6.

decisions.choice: bend justice / make the outcome unfair
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves the object of "thrust aside" unstated; Balanced and Readable supply it. Literal brackets "justice".

records.source: וְדָ֕ל לֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And a poor [person] not you must honor in his case at law.
pieces: Do not give special treatment to {{gender:a poor person|a poor man}} in {{gender:their|his}} lawsuit either.

L.3: And a poor [one] you shall not favor in his lawsuit.

R.3: In court, do not take a poor person's side out of pity.

decisions.choice: do not favor a poor man: justice must not lean even toward the weak
decisions.reason: The verb means to honor or show regard. A judge or witness must not tilt a case toward a poor man because he is poor, just as he must not tilt it toward the crowd (verse 2). Leviticus 19:15 forbids both: favoring the poor and deferring to the great.

decisions.choice: poor: the reading of the Hebrew text
alternatives: do not favor a great man in his lawsuit
decisions.reason: The Hebrew manuscripts read "poor". A change of one letter would give "great", and Leviticus 19:15 names the poor and the great side by side, so some have proposed reading "a great man" here. That reading is a conjecture, not one found in a Hebrew manuscript; and verse 6 shows the law guarding the poor from both sides.

decisions.choice: out of pity
decisions.reason: Readable names the reason such favor would be shown, to make the point of the law clear.

records.source: כִּ֣י תִפְגַּ֞ע שׁ֧וֹר אֹֽיִבְךָ֛ א֥וֹ חֲמֹר֖וֹ תֹּעֶ֑ה הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֶ֖נּוּ לֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: If you meet the ox of your enemy or his donkey wandering off, certainly you will return it to him.
pieces: When you find your enemy's ox or donkey gone astray, you must lead it back to its owner.

L.4: If you meet your enemy's ox or his donkey wandering off, you shall surely return it to him.

R.4: Suppose you find your enemy's ox or donkey wandering loose. You must take it back to its owner.

decisions.choice: your enemy's ox: help is owed even to an enemy
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 22:1-4 gives the same law for a "brother". Here it reaches to one's enemy, perhaps an opponent at law, set as it is among laws about the courts. Being in a dispute with someone does not excuse leaving his animal to be lost (compare Proverbs 25:21).

decisions.choice: its owner
decisions.reason: "To him" means the enemy who owns the animal; Balanced and Readable say "its owner".

records.source: כִּֽי־תִרְאֶ֞ה חֲמ֣וֹר שֹׂנַאֲךָ֗ רֹבֵץ֙ תַּ֣חַת מַשָּׂא֔וֹ וְחָדַלְתָּ֖ מֵעֲזֹ֣ב ל֑וֹ עָזֹ֥ב תַּעֲזֹ֖ב עִמּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: If you see the donkey of [one who] hates you lying down under its load, and you will refrain from leaving it to him, certainly you will rearrange [it] with him.
pieces: Suppose the donkey of someone who hates you has sunk down under its burden. However much you may wish to leave it to {{gender:them|him}}, you must work with {{gender:them|him}} to set it free.

L.5: If you see the donkey of one who hates you lying under its load, and you would hold back from leaving [it] to {{gender:them|him}}, you shall surely help with {{gender:them|him}}.

R.5: You may see the donkey of someone who hates you lying on the ground under a heavy load. You might not want to help, but you must help that person get the donkey up again.

decisions.choice: leaving ... help: the same verb used two ways
alternatives: you shall surely leave it with him (unload it together)
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to leave or abandon, and the first time it has that sense: you may want to leave the animal to its owner. The second time it must mean the opposite, to help or set free, perhaps a second verb of the same sound meaning to arrange or put right (compare Nehemiah 3:8). The play on words sets what one would like to do against what one must do. Deuteronomy 22:4 gives the same law with the plain verb "lift up".

decisions.choice: and you would hold back: a concession
decisions.reason: The clause is best taken as a concession: even if you would rather refrain from helping, you must help. Some take it as a command ("refrain from leaving it"), with the same result.

decisions.choice: get the donkey up again
decisions.reason: Readable says what the help is: getting the fallen animal back on its feet.

records.source: לֹ֥א תַטֶּ֛ה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט אֶבְיֹנְךָ֖ בְּרִיבֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Not you must turn aside the justice of your needy [person] in his case at law.
pieces: Do not pervert the justice due to your poor when they bring a case.

L.6: You shall not turn aside the justice of your needy [one] in his lawsuit.

R.6: When poor people among you go to court, do not twist the law against them.

decisions.choice: turn aside the justice of your needy: deny the poor the verdict they are owed
decisions.reason: To turn justice aside is to bend a case away from what is right (Deuteronomy 16:19; 24:17; Amos 5:12). "Your needy" are the poor of your own people. Verse 3 kept the court from favoring the poor; this verse keeps it from wronging them.

decisions.choice: your poor / poor people among you
decisions.reason: "Your needy one" is collective; Balanced and Readable use the plural.

records.heading: Justice, rest and the yearly feasts

records.source: מִדְּבַר־שֶׁ֖קֶר תִּרְחָ֑ק וְנָקִ֤י וְצַדִּיק֙ אַֽל־תַּהֲרֹ֔ג כִּ֥י לֹא־אַצְדִּ֖יק רָשָֽׁע׃
records.gloss: From a word of falsehood you will be distant, and an innocent [person] and a righteous [person] do not kill, for not I will declare righteous a wicked [person].
pieces: Stay far away from a false charge. Do not put to death one who is innocent and in the right, for I will not declare the wicked to be in the right.

L.7: From a false matter you shall keep far; and the innocent and the righteous do not kill, for I will not justify the wicked.

R.7: Have nothing to do with lies in court. Do not cause the death of an innocent person who has done nothing wrong. I will not treat the guilty as if they were innocent.

decisions.choice: a false matter: a false charge or false testimony in a case
decisions.reason: The word can mean a word or a matter. In this setting it is a false accusation or a lying statement in court.

decisions.choice: do not kill the innocent: by a false case or an unjust verdict
decisions.reason: The innocent and the one in the right are killed here through the court, when false testimony or a bent judgment brings a death sentence (1 Kings 21:8-13).

decisions.choice: I will not justify the wicked: God's own judgment stands behind the court's
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare in the right, the language of a verdict. If a human court acquits the guilty, God will not (Proverbs 17:15; 34:7).

records.source: וְשֹׁ֖חַד לֹ֣א תִקָּ֑ח כִּ֤י הַשֹּׁ֨חַד֙ יְעַוֵּ֣ר פִּקְחִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽים׃
records.gloss: And a bribe not you must take, for the bribe makes blind clear-sighted [people] and perverts [the] words of righteous [people].
pieces: Take no bribe. A bribe blinds the clear-sighted and overturns the cause of those who are in the right.

L.8: And a bribe you shall not take, for the bribe blinds the clear-sighted and subverts the words of the righteous.

R.8: Never accept money or gifts to change your decision. Bribes keep even wise people from seeing clearly, and they twist the case of people who are in the right.

decisions.choice: blinds the clear-sighted: corrupts even those who see well
decisions.reason: The clear-sighted are those whose eyes are open: wise and fair judges. A bribe takes away the very sight they have (Deuteronomy 16:19).

decisions.choice: the words of the righteous: the case of those in the right
decisions.reason: The words of the righteous may be the pleas of the innocent party, which a bribe overturns, or the rulings of honest judges, which a bribe twists. The first fits the courtroom setting of verses 6-7.

decisions.choice: money or gifts to change your decision
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a bribe is.

records.source: וְגֵ֖ר לֹ֣א תִלְחָ֑ץ וְאַתֶּ֗ם יְדַעְתֶּם֙ אֶת־נֶ֣פֶשׁ הַגֵּ֔ר כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And a sojourner not you must oppress, and you, you have known the life of the sojourner, for sojourners you were in [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Do not oppress a foreigner living among you. You know from the inside what a foreigner's life is like, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

L.9: And a sojourner you shall not oppress; for you, you know the life of the sojourner, for you were sojourners in the land of Egypt.

R.9: Do not be cruel to foreigners who live among you. You know what it is like to live in a land that is not your own. You lived that way in Egypt.

decisions.choice: you know the life (soul) of the sojourner: you know from experience what it is to be one
decisions.reason: The word often rendered "soul" means the life or inner self of a person, with its needs and longings. Israel knows the stranger's life from within, having lived it in Egypt.

decisions.choice: the law of 22:20 repeated
decisions.reason: 22:20 gave the same command with the same reason. Here it closes the laws about the courts: a foreigner, who had no family to stand for him, must not be wronged in a case (Deuteronomy 24:17).

decisions.choice: foreigner living among you
decisions.reason: As in 12:19 and 12:48. Literal keeps "sojourner".

records.source: וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים תִּזְרַ֣ע אֶת־אַרְצֶ֑ךָ וְאָסַפְתָּ֖ אֶת־תְּבוּאָתָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And six years you will sow your land and you will gather its produce,
pieces: For six years you are to sow your land and gather in its crops,

L.10: And six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce,

R.10: For six years, plant your fields and harvest the crops.

decisions.choice: six years: the pattern of the week applied to the land
decisions.reason: The six years of sowing and the seventh year of rest (verse 11) follow the six days of work and the seventh day of rest (verse 12; 20:9-10). Leviticus 25:1-7 gives the law of the land's Sabbath year at greater length.

records.source: וְהַשְּׁבִיעִ֞ת תִּשְׁמְטֶ֣נָּה וּנְטַשְׁתָּ֗הּ וְאָֽכְלוּ֙ אֶבְיֹנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְיִתְרָ֕ם תֹּאכַ֖ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה כֵּֽן־תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה לְכַרְמְךָ֖ לְזֵיתֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: and the seventh [year] you will let it rest and you will leave it fallow, and they will eat, the needy [people] of your people, and their excess will eat the animal[s] of the field. Thus you will do to your vineyard, to your olive grove.
pieces: but in the seventh you are to release it and let it lie, so that the needy among your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what they leave. Treat your vineyard and your olive grove the same way.

L.11: but the seventh [year] you shall let it drop and leave it, and the needy of your people shall eat, and what they leave the animal[s] of the field shall eat. So you shall do to your vineyard, to your olive grove.

R.11: But in the seventh year, do not plant or harvest. Let the land rest. Poor people may eat whatever grows there, and wild animals may eat what is left. Do this with your grapevines and olive trees too.

decisions.choice: let it drop and leave it: release the land from work and let it lie
decisions.reason: The first verb means to let fall or release; it is used of the release of debts in the seventh year (Deuteronomy 15:2). The second means to leave alone. The land is not sown, and what grows of itself is not harvested for the owner.

decisions.choice: the needy and the wild animals eat: the rest serves the poor and the creatures
decisions.reason: The seventh year is not only rest for the soil; what grows of itself belongs to the poor of the people, and what they leave to the animals (Leviticus 25:6-7).

decisions.choice: do not plant or harvest
decisions.reason: Readable says what letting the land rest means in practice.

records.source: שֵׁ֤שֶׁת יָמִים֙ תַּעֲשֶׂ֣ה מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ וּבַיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י תִּשְׁבֹּ֑ת לְמַ֣עַן יָנ֗וּחַ שֽׁוֹרְךָ֙ וַחֲמֹרֶ֔ךָ וְיִנָּפֵ֥שׁ בֶּן־אֲמָתְךָ֖ וְהַגֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: Six days you will do your work(s), and on the day the seventh you will rest, so that it may rest, your ox and your donkey, and he will refresh himself, the child of your female slave and the sojourner.
pieces: Work for six days, but on the seventh day stop, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the {{gender:child|son}} of your female servant and the foreigner living among you may be refreshed.

L.12: Six days you shall do your works, and on the seventh day you shall cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the {{gender:child|son}} of your slave woman and the sojourner may be refreshed.

R.12: Do your work in six days, but stop working on the seventh day. Then your ox and your donkey can rest. The {{gender:child|son}} of your female servant and the foreigner who lives with you can rest and get their strength back.

decisions.choice: six days ... on the seventh day you shall cease: the Sabbath command repeated
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which the word Sabbath comes. The command of 20:8-11 is given again here, with its reason turned toward the weak: the animals, the slave and the foreigner.

decisions.choice: be refreshed: catch one's breath, be revived
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for breath or life. It is used of God himself resting on the seventh day (31:17) and of a weary man reviving (2 Samuel 16:14).

decisions.choice: the son of your slave woman: a slave born in the household
decisions.reason: The son of a slave woman was himself born a slave in the household (Genesis 14:14; Psalm 116:16). He, too, is given the day of rest.

decisions.choice: female servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave". The meaning decision (m3) keeps that her son was born a slave in the household.

records.source: וּבְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־אָמַ֥רְתִּי אֲלֵיכֶ֖ם תִּשָּׁמֵ֑רוּ וְשֵׁ֨ם אֱלֹהִ֤ים אֲחֵרִים֙ לֹ֣א תַזְכִּ֔ירוּ לֹ֥א יִשָּׁמַ֖ע עַל־פִּֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And in all that I have said to you, you will take heed; and [the] name of other gods not you will bring to remembrance; not it will be heard on your mouth.
pieces: Be on guard in all that I have said to you. Do not make mention of the names of other gods; let no such name be heard from your mouth.

L.13: And in all that I have said to you take heed; and the name of other gods you shall not mention; it shall not be heard on your mouth.

R.13: Be careful to obey everything I have told you. Do not pray to other gods or even say their names.

decisions.choice: do not make mention of the name of other gods: do not call on them or speak of them with honor
decisions.reason: To "cause to remember" a name is to call on it, swear by it or praise it (Joshua 23:7; Psalm 20:8). Israel is not to call on other gods in worship or oath; the command guards the first commandment (20:3).

decisions.choice: in all that I have said: the whole of the law just given
decisions.reason: The sentence closes the laws of 20:22-23:12 before the laws of the feasts. Heeding all that God has said comes first; turning from other gods sums it up.

decisions.choice: pray to ... or even say their names
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what making mention of a god's name involves: calling on it in prayer, and speaking it at all.

records.source: שָׁלֹ֣שׁ רְגָלִ֔ים תָּחֹ֥ג לִ֖י בַּשָּׁנָֽה׃
records.gloss: Three feet you will celebrate a festival to me in the year.
pieces: Three times each year you shall keep a pilgrim feast in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} honor.

L.14: Three times you shall keep a feast to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} in the year.

R.14: Each year you must hold three festivals to honor {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

decisions.choice: three feet: three times
decisions.reason: The word for "feet" is used here for "times" (Numbers 22:28), perhaps because each feast meant a journey on foot to the place of worship. Verse 17 says the same with the usual word for "times".

decisions.choice: keep a feast: hold a pilgrim festival
decisions.reason: The verb means to hold a festival, often with a journey to the sanctuary; it is the verb Moses used when asking Pharaoh to let the people go to hold a feast in the wilderness (5:1; 10:9).

decisions.choice: pilgrim feast
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "pilgrim" to show that these feasts were kept by going to worship at the sanctuary (verse 17).

records.source: אֶת־חַ֣ג הַמַּצּוֹת֮ תִּשְׁמֹר֒ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִים֩ תֹּאכַ֨ל מַצּ֜וֹת כַּֽאֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֗ךָ לְמוֹעֵד֙ חֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽאָבִ֔יב כִּי־ב֖וֹ יָצָ֣אתָ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְלֹא־יֵרָא֥וּ פָנַ֖י רֵיקָֽם׃
records.gloss: The festival of the unleavened bread(s) you will keep; seven days you will eat unleavened bread(s), just as I commanded you, at the appointed time [of] the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And not they will present themselves [before] my presence empty.
pieces: Observe the Feast of Unleavened Bread: you shall eat unleavened bread seven days, as I instructed you, at its fixed time in the month of Abib, the month when you left Egypt. And let no one come into {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} presence empty-handed.

L.15: The Feast of Unleavened Bread you shall keep; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time [in] the month of Abib, for in it you came out from Egypt. And none shall appear before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} empty.

R.15: First, celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat unleavened bread made without yeast, as I told you. Do this at the time I set in the month of Abib, in early spring, because that is when you left Egypt. Everyone who comes before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} must bring a gift.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Unleavened Bread in Abib: the feast commanded in 12:15-20 and 13:3-10
decisions.reason: Abib, "fresh ears of grain", is the spring month in which Israel left Egypt (13:4). The seven days of unleavened bread follow the Passover (12:15-20).

decisions.choice: none shall appear before me empty: no one is to come to worship without an offering
alternatives: none shall see my face empty-handed
decisions.reason: The verb form as the Hebrew text is pointed means "be seen" or "appear" before God's face. The same consonants could be read "see my face", and some think that was the first reading, later softened. Either way the worshiper comes into God's presence and must not come with nothing to offer (34:20; Deuteronomy 16:16-17).

decisions.choice: First ... in early spring
decisions.reason: Readable numbers the three feasts of verses 15-16 and places Abib in the year, as in 13:4.

records.source: וְחַ֤ג הַקָּצִיר֙ בִּכּוּרֵ֣י מַעֲשֶׂ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר תִּזְרַ֖ע בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וְחַ֤ג הָֽאָסִף֙ בְּצֵ֣את הַשָּׁנָ֔ה בְּאָסְפְּךָ֥ אֶֽת־מַעֲשֶׂ֖יךָ מִן־הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And the festival of the harvest, the first-fruits of your works which you will sow in [the] field, and the festival of the ingathering when goes out the year, when you have gathered your works from the field.
pieces: Keep also the Feast of Harvest, with the firstfruits of your labor, of what you sow in the field, and the Feast of Ingathering at the turn of the year, when you gather in from the field what your labor has produced.

L.16: And the Feast of Harvest, the firstfruits of your works, which you sow in the field; and the Feast of Ingathering at the going out of the year, when you gather in your works from the field.

R.16: Second, celebrate the Festival of Harvest when the first crops you planted are ready. Third, celebrate the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the growing year, when you bring in your crops from the fields.

decisions.choice: the Feast of Harvest: the wheat harvest, later called the Feast of Weeks
decisions.reason: This is the feast of the first of the grain harvest, called the Feast of Weeks in 34:22 and Deuteronomy 16:9-10, seven weeks after the start of the harvest (Leviticus 23:15-17).

decisions.choice: the Feast of Ingathering at the going out of the year: the autumn feast, later called Booths
decisions.reason: The last harvest of fruit, grapes and olives was gathered in autumn, at the close of the farming year. The feast is called the Feast of Booths in Leviticus 23:34-43 and Deuteronomy 16:13. "The going out of the year" means the end of the year's work in the fields; 34:22 calls it "the turn of the year".

decisions.choice: Second ... Third ... growing year
decisions.reason: Readable numbers the feasts and makes clear that the year meant is the farming year.

records.source: שָׁלֹ֥שׁ פְּעָמִ֖ים בַּשָּׁנָ֑ה יֵרָאֶה֙ כָּל־זְכ֣וּרְךָ֔ אֶל־פְּנֵ֖י הָאָדֹ֥ן׀יְהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Three times in the year he will present himself, every male of yours, to the presence of the lord Yahweh.
pieces: Three times a year every male among you is to present himself before the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

L.17: Three times in the year all your males shall appear before the face of the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

R.17: Three times every year, all your men and boys must come and stand before the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: the Lord Yahweh: the divine name with the title "Lord" before it
decisions.reason: "Lord" is the title of a master or sovereign; joined to the divine name it calls Yahweh Israel's master, to whom the people come as servants three times a year (34:23).

decisions.choice: all your males: the men were required to come
decisions.reason: The duty to come to the sanctuary was laid on the males. Women and children often came as well (Deuteronomy 16:11, 14; 1 Samuel 1:3-7).

decisions.choice: the Lord GOD
decisions.reason: Where the title "Lord" comes just before the divine name, "GOD" in capitals marks the name, to avoid "Lord LORD".

records.source: לֹֽא־תִזְבַּ֥ח עַל־חָמֵ֖ץ דַּם־זִבְחִ֑י וְלֹֽא־יָלִ֥ין חֵֽלֶב־חַגִּ֖י עַד־בֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: Not you must sacrifice with leaven the blood of my sacrifice, and not it will remain overnight, the fat of my festival sacrifice, until morning.
pieces: Do not offer the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice with anything leavened, and the fat from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feast must not be left over until morning.

L.18: You shall not sacrifice the blood of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sacrifice with leaven; and the fat of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} feast shall not remain overnight until morning.

R.18: When you offer an animal to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, do not offer bread made with yeast along with its blood. And do not keep the fat from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} festival sacrifices until the next morning.

decisions.choice: the blood of my sacrifice with leaven: no leavened bread with a blood sacrifice
decisions.reason: Leaven was kept away from the altar (Leviticus 2:11). In 34:25 the same law is tied to the Passover sacrifice, which was eaten with unleavened bread (12:8).

decisions.choice: the fat of my feast: the fat of the festival sacrifice
decisions.reason: "My feast" stands for the sacrifice offered at the feast. Its fat belonged to God and was to be burned on the altar the same night, not left over (Leviticus 3:16; 7:15). In 34:25 the parallel speaks of the Passover sacrifice.

decisions.choice: When you offer an animal to me ... bread made with yeast
decisions.reason: Readable explains the sacrifice and the leaven.

records.source: רֵאשִׁ֗ית בִּכּוּרֵי֙ אַדְמָ֣תְךָ֔ תָּבִ֕יא בֵּ֖ית יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֑יךָ לֹֽא־תְבַשֵּׁ֥ל גְּדִ֖י בַּחֲלֵ֥ב אִמּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: The first of the first-fruits of your ground you will bring [to] the house of Yahweh your God. Not you must boil a kid in the milk of its mother.
pieces: The best of your ground's firstfruits you are to bring to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.

L.19: The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring [to the] house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk.

R.19: Bring the best of the first crops from your land to the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. Do not cook a young goat in milk from its own mother.

decisions.choice: the first of the firstfruits: the best and earliest of the crop
decisions.reason: The first word can mean the first in time or the first in quality, the best (Numbers 18:12). Both senses fit: the earliest and choicest produce belongs to God.

decisions.choice: the house of Yahweh: the place where God is worshiped
decisions.reason: No temple yet existed. The house of Yahweh is the sanctuary God will choose, first the tabernacle (25:8) and later the temple (Deuteronomy 26:2).

decisions.choice: do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk: the reason is uncertain
decisions.reason: The law is given three times (here; 34:26; Deuteronomy 14:21) with no reason stated. It may forbid a practice of other peoples' worship, or it may teach respect for the bond between mother and young, like Leviticus 22:28 and Deuteronomy 22:6-7. Its placement here, with the firstfruits, ties it to the harvest feasts.

records.source: הִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י שֹׁלֵ֤חַ מַלְאָךְ֙ לְפָנֶ֔יךָ לִשְׁמָרְךָ֖ בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וְלַהֲבִ֣יאֲךָ֔ אֶל־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֲכִנֹֽתִי׃
records.gloss: Here! I [am] about to send an angel before you to guard you on the journey and to bring you into the place which I have prepared.
pieces: I am sending an angel to go before you. He will protect you on your journey and lead you to the place I have made ready.

L.20: Look, I am sending an angel before you to guard you on the way and to bring you into the place that I have prepared.

R.20: I am sending an angel in front of you. He will keep you safe on the road and bring you to the place I have made ready for you.

decisions.choice: an angel (messenger): a messenger sent by God
decisions.reason: The word means a messenger, human or heavenly. Here it is God's messenger who goes before Israel, as "the angel of God" went before the camp at the sea (14:19). In 32:34 and 33:2 God again promises to send an angel before them.

decisions.choice: the place I have prepared: the land of Canaan
decisions.reason: The place is the land God promised (verse 23; 3:8). Moses' song speaks of the place God made for his dwelling (15:17).

decisions.choice: "Look" left out
decisions.reason: Balanced drops "look" here and begins with God's announcement; Literal keeps it.

records.heading: An angel to lead the way

records.source: הִשָּׁ֧מֶר מִפָּנָ֛יו וּשְׁמַ֥ע בְּקֹל֖וֹ אַל־תַּמֵּ֣ר בּ֑וֹ כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יִשָּׂא֙ לְפִשְׁעֲכֶ֔ם כִּ֥י שְׁמִ֖י בְּקִרְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: Take care before him and listen to his voice; do not cause bitterness in him, for not he will forgive your transgression, for my name [is] within him.
pieces: Take care in his presence and obey what he says. Do not defy him, because he will not pardon your wrongdoing; {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is in him.

L.21: Take heed before him and listen to his voice; do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your transgression, for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name [is] in him.

R.21: Be careful to respect him and do what he tells you. Do not turn against him. He will not overlook your sins, because {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} name is in him.

decisions.choice: do not rebel against him: do not provoke or defy him
decisions.reason: The verb is from a root meaning to be bitter or to rebel; to embitter someone is to provoke him by defiance. Israel would do this in the wilderness (Psalm 78:40, 56).

decisions.choice: my name is in him: he bears God's own presence and authority
decisions.reason: God's name stands for God himself as he makes himself known (3:15; 20:24). The angel acts with God's full authority and presence, so to defy him is to defy God. Some see in this angel God himself appearing (compare 3:2-6; 33:14-15); the verse does not say.

decisions.choice: he will not pardon your transgression: rebellion will not be passed over
decisions.reason: The verb means to lift or bear, here to forgive. The warning is that defying the angel is defying God.

records.source: כִּ֣י אִם־שָׁמֹ֤עַ תִּשְׁמַע֙ בְּקֹל֔וֹ וְעָשִׂ֕יתָ כֹּ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֲדַבֵּ֑ר וְאָֽיַבְתִּי֙ אֶת־אֹ֣יְבֶ֔יךָ וְצַרְתִּ֖י אֶת־צֹרְרֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: For if carefully you will listen to his voice and you will do all that I will say, and I will be an enemy to your enemies and I will treat as a foe your foes.
pieces: If you truly heed his voice and do everything I tell you, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and an adversary to those who stand against you.

L.22: For if you surely listen to his voice and do all that I say, then I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.

R.22: If you listen closely to him and do all I tell you, I will fight against your enemies and stand against all who attack you.

decisions.choice: listen to his voice ... all that I say: the angel's word is God's word
decisions.reason: Obeying the angel's voice is doing what God says; the two are one (verse 21).

decisions.choice: I will be an enemy to your enemies: God takes Israel's side
decisions.reason: The promise echoes God's word to Abraham (Genesis 12:3). The two verbs are a pair: Israel's enemies and foes become God's.

records.source: כִּֽי־יֵלֵ֣ךְ מַלְאָכִי֮ לְפָנֶיךָ֒ וֶהֱבִֽיאֲךָ֗ אֶל־הָֽאֱמֹרִי֙ וְהַ֣חִתִּ֔י וְהַפְּרִזִּי֙ וְהַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י הַחִוִּ֖י וְהַיְבוּסִ֑י וְהִכְחַדְתִּֽיו׃
records.gloss: For he will go, my angel, before you and he will bring you to the Amorite[s] and the Hittite[s] and the Perizzite[s] and the Canaanite[s], the Hivite[s] and the Jebusite[s], and I will annihilate it.
pieces: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel will go before you and bring you to the land of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will make an end of them.

L.23: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} angel will go before you and bring you to the Amorites and the Hittites and the Perizzites and the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.

R.23: My angel will lead you into the land where the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites live. And I will destroy those nations.

decisions.choice: the peoples of Canaan: the nations named in the promise to the fathers
decisions.reason: The list repeats the peoples named when God first spoke to Moses (3:8, 17; compare Genesis 15:19-21).

decisions.choice: I will wipe them out: I will destroy them as nations
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off or efface. Its object is singular, gathering the nations into one. Verses 28-30 show this done by driving them out little by little.

decisions.choice: the land of
decisions.reason: The angel brings Israel to these peoples' land; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: לֹֽא־תִשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֤ה לֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶם֙ וְלֹ֣א תָֽעָבְדֵ֔ם וְלֹ֥א תַעֲשֶׂ֖ה כְּמַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם כִּ֤י הָרֵס֙ תְּהָ֣רְסֵ֔ם וְשַׁבֵּ֥ר תְּשַׁבֵּ֖ר מַצֵּבֹתֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Not you must bow down to their gods and not you must be enticed to serve them, and not you must make like their works, for completely you will tear them down and totally you will shatter into pieces their sacred pillars.
pieces: Do not bow down to their gods or serve them, and do not copy what they do. Instead, you are to pull those gods down completely and break their sacred pillars into pieces.

L.24: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their works; but you shall utterly tear them down and smash their pillars to pieces.

R.24: Do not bow down to their gods or worship them. Do not do the things those nations do. Instead, tear down their idols completely and smash the stone pillars they worship.

decisions.choice: do according to their works: follow the peoples' religious practices
decisions.reason: Their works are what the Canaanite peoples did in worship of their gods (Leviticus 18:3).

decisions.choice: tear them down: their gods, that is, their images
decisions.reason: "Them" most naturally refers to "their gods" at the start of the verse, meaning the images and shrines that stood for those gods (34:13; Deuteronomy 7:5).

decisions.choice: pillars: standing stones set up for worship
decisions.reason: These were stones set upright as markers of a god's presence at a shrine. Israel had once set up such stones to God (Genesis 28:18; Exodus 24:4), but Canaanite pillars were to be smashed (Deuteronomy 12:3).

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving other gods.

records.source: וַעֲבַדְתֶּ֗ם אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵרַ֥ךְ אֶֽת־לַחְמְךָ֖ וְאֶת־מֵימֶ֑יךָ וַהֲסִרֹתִ֥י מַחֲלָ֖ה מִקִּרְבֶּֽךָ׃
records.gloss: And you will serve Yahweh your God, and he will bless your food and your water, and I will remove sickness from your midst.
pieces: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from among you.

L.25: And you shall serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your bread and your water; and I will remove sickness from your midst.

R.25: Worship {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will bless your food and water. I will take disease away from you.

decisions.choice: he will bless ... I will remove: God speaks of himself in the third person and then the first
decisions.reason: The change of person is common in God's speeches in the law and does not mean a different speaker (compare verse 19). The ancient Greek translation reads "I will bless"; this note comes from memory and should be checked.

decisions.choice: I will remove sickness: God as Israel's healer
decisions.reason: The promise recalls 15:26, where God said he would put none of the diseases of Egypt on Israel, for "I am Yahweh your healer".

decisions.choice: Worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving God here.

records.source: לֹ֥א תִהְיֶ֛ה מְשַׁכֵּלָ֥ה וַעֲקָרָ֖ה בְּאַרְצֶ֑ךָ אֶת־מִסְפַּ֥ר יָמֶ֖יךָ אֲמַלֵּֽא׃
records.gloss: Not anyone will be miscarrying and barren in your land; the number of your days I will complete.
pieces: No woman in your land will lose her child before birth or be unable to bear children. I will let you live out the full number of your days.

L.26: There shall not be [one] miscarrying or barren in your land; the number of your days I will fill.

R.26: No woman in your land will lose a baby before it is born, and none will be unable to have children. I will give you long, full lives.

decisions.choice: miscarrying or barren: women who lose their young or cannot bear
decisions.reason: Both words are feminine. The first is used of losing young before birth (Genesis 31:38), the second of a woman who cannot conceive (Genesis 11:30). The promise reaches to the flocks as well (Deuteronomy 7:14).

decisions.choice: I will fill the number of your days: you will live a full life
decisions.reason: God will let his people reach the full span of life, not be cut off early (Psalm 55:24; Isaiah 65:20).

records.source: אֶת־אֵֽימָתִי֙ אֲשַׁלַּ֣ח לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְהַמֹּתִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖א בָּהֶ֑ם וְנָתַתִּ֧י אֶת־כָּל־אֹיְבֶ֛יךָ אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֹֽרֶף׃
records.gloss: My terror I will send before you, and I will confuse every people among whom you will go, and I will give all your enemies to you [as] neck.
pieces: I will send terror of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} ahead of you and throw every people you come against into panic. I will make all your enemies show you their backs.

L.27: My terror I will send before you, and I will throw into confusion all the people among whom you come, and I will make all your enemies [turn their] neck to you.

R.27: I will make the nations afraid of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} before you arrive. I will cause panic among every people you go up against, and all your enemies will turn and run from you.

decisions.choice: my terror: the dread God sends on the nations
decisions.reason: It is the fear of God that seizes Israel's enemies before battle, as Moses' song foretold (15:14-16; Joshua 2:9-11).

decisions.choice: throw into confusion: put into panic
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God putting an army into panic in battle (14:24; Joshua 10:10).

decisions.choice: give your enemies to you as a neck: make them turn their backs and flee
decisions.reason: To show someone the back of the neck is to turn and run (2 Samuel 22:41; Psalm 18:41).

records.source: וְשָׁלַחְתִּ֥י אֶת־הַצִּרְעָ֖ה לְפָנֶ֑יךָ וְגֵרְשָׁ֗ה אֶת־הַחִוִּ֧י אֶת־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י וְאֶת־הַחִתִּ֖י מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivite[s], the Canaanite[s] and the Hittite[s] from before you.
pieces: I will send the hornet in front of you, and it will chase the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites out of your path.

L.28: And I will send the hornet before you, and it will drive out the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites from before you.

R.28: I will send hornets ahead of you. They will chase away the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites as you come.

decisions.choice: the hornet: the meaning of the word is uncertain
decisions.reason: The word appears only here, in Deuteronomy 7:20 and in Joshua 24:12, each time of something God sends to drive out the peoples of Canaan. It is usually taken as "hornet", a stinging insect, either real or a picture of a terror that drives people to flight. Others understand it as "discouragement" or "panic", in line with verse 27. Joshua 24:12 says it was not by Israel's sword or bow.

decisions.choice: the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites: three of the peoples of verse 23, standing for all
decisions.reason: Three names stand for the whole list.

records.source: לֹ֧א אֲגָרְשֶׁ֛נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ בְּשָׁנָ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת פֶּן־תִּהְיֶ֤ה הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ שְׁמָמָ֔ה וְרַבָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יךָ חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: Not I will drive it out from before you in a year one, lest it should become, the land, a waste, and it will become many on you, the animal[s] of the field.
pieces: Yet I will not clear them away from before you within one year. If I did, the land would lie empty, and the wild animals would multiply and overrun you.

L.29: I will not drive them out from before you in one year, lest the land become a desolation and the animal[s] of the field multiply against you.

R.29: But I will not force them all out in one year. If I did, much of the land would be left empty, and wild animals would increase and become a danger to you.

decisions.choice: not in one year: God's care in the pace of the conquest
decisions.reason: The gradual driving out is not a failure of God's power but care for his people: an emptied land would go wild before Israel could fill it (Deuteronomy 7:22). Judges 2:20-3:4 gives a further reason why some peoples remained.

decisions.choice: the animal of the field: wild animals
decisions.reason: The phrase means wild beasts, which multiply where people are few (2 Kings 17:25-26).

records.source: מְעַ֥ט מְעַ֛ט אֲגָרְשֶׁ֖נּוּ מִפָּנֶ֑יךָ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּפְרֶ֔ה וְנָחַלְתָּ֖ אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: Little little I will drive it out from before you, until that you will be fruitful and you will possess the land.
pieces: I will drive them out from before you little by little, until you have grown many and can take the land as your own.

L.30: Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you are fruitful and possess the land.

R.30: I will push them out a little at a time, until there are enough of you to take over the whole land.

decisions.choice: little by little: a little at a time
decisions.reason: The word "little" is doubled to mean bit by bit, a stage at a time (Deuteronomy 7:22).

decisions.choice: be fruitful and possess: grow in number and take the land as an inheritance
decisions.reason: "Be fruitful" echoes the blessing of Genesis 1:28 and the growth of Israel in Egypt (1:7). The second verb means to receive as an inheritance.

records.source: וְשַׁתִּ֣י אֶת־גְּבֻלְךָ֗ מִיַּם־סוּף֙ וְעַד־יָ֣ם פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וּמִמִּדְבָּ֖ר עַד־הַנָּהָ֑ר כִּ֣י׀אֶתֵּ֣ן בְּיֶדְכֶ֗ם אֵ֚ת יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ וְגֵרַשְׁתָּ֖מוֹ מִפָּנֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And I will set your border from [the] sea of reed[s] and to the sea of [the] Philistines, and from [the] wilderness to the River; for I will give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and you will drive them out from before you.
pieces: I will fix your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the Euphrates River. I will hand over to you the people who live in the land, and you will drive them out before you.

L.31: And I will set your border from the Sea of Reeds to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River; for I will give into your hand the inhabitants of the land, and you shall drive them out from before you.

R.31: Your land will stretch from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean Sea, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I will put the people who live there in your power, and you will force them out as you advance.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: here the gulf on the southeast of the land
decisions.reason: See the note at 10:19 on the name. Here, at the southern edge of the promised land, it most likely means the gulf east of Sinai, on whose shore Ezion-geber stood (1 Kings 9:26).

decisions.choice: the sea of the Philistines ... the wilderness ... the River: the Mediterranean, the southern desert and the Euphrates
decisions.reason: The sea of the Philistines is the Mediterranean, on whose coast the Philistines lived. The wilderness is the desert to the south, and "the River" here is the Euphrates, as in the promise to Abraham (Genesis 15:18; Deuteronomy 11:24; 1 Kings 5:1).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Elsewhere in Exodus "the River" is the Nile; here it is the Euphrates, so Balanced and Readable name it. Readable also names the Mediterranean for "the sea of the Philistines". Literal keeps "the River".

records.source: לֹֽא־תִכְרֹ֥ת לָהֶ֛ם וְלֵאלֹֽהֵיהֶ֖ם בְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: Not you must make with them and with their gods a covenant.
pieces: Make no covenant with them or with their gods.

L.32: You shall not make with them or with their gods a covenant.

R.32: Do not make any agreement with those peoples or with their gods.

decisions.choice: no covenant with them or their gods: Israel belongs to one covenant only
decisions.reason: A treaty with the peoples of Canaan would bind Israel to their gods as well, since such treaties were sworn by the gods of both sides. Israel is bound to Yahweh alone (34:12, 15; Deuteronomy 7:2; Joshua 9).

decisions.choice: agreement
decisions.reason: Readable says "agreement" for a covenant between peoples.

records.source: לֹ֤א יֵשְׁבוּ֙ בְּאַרְצְךָ֔ פֶּן־יַחֲטִ֥יאוּ אֹתְךָ֖ לִ֑י כִּ֤י תַעֲבֹד֙ אֶת־אֱלֹ֣הֵיהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֖ לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃פ
records.gloss: Not they will dwell in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me, for you will serve their gods, for it will become for you a snare.
pieces: They must not live in your land, or they will lead you to sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. For you would come to serve their gods, and that would be a snare to you."

L.33: They shall not dwell in your land, lest they make you sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; for you will serve their gods, for it will be a snare to you."

R.33: Do not let them stay in your land. They would lead you to sin against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You would begin to worship their gods, and that would catch you like a trap."

decisions.choice: for you will serve their gods, for it will be a snare: the danger explained
alternatives: if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you
decisions.reason: The two clauses may be read as cause and result ("for you would serve their gods, and that would be a snare") or as a condition ("if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare"). Either way the presence of these peoples leads to their worship, and their worship to ruin (34:12; Judges 2:3).

decisions.choice: a snare: a trap that catches its prey
decisions.reason: The word is a hunter's trap. The worship of other gods would catch Israel and bring it down (Deuteronomy 7:16; Psalm 106:36).

decisions.choice: the end of God's words
decisions.reason: The speech that began at 20:22 ends here; in 24:1 the narrative takes up again.

decisions.choice: worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for serving other gods.
